subject: Helion Health - dedicated SLO & GPU sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@helionhealth.com>, Marco Bianco <marco.bianco@helionhealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Helion Health - dedicated SLO & GPU sizing follow-up

Hi Maya / Marco —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum for the dedicated-capacity PoC.

Call summary (high level)
- Goal: Move latency-sensitive summarization and assisted charting workflows to a dedicated Redwood pool for predictable p95 latency and streaming token delivery.
- Target SLOs: p95 generation latency <= 150ms for short interactions (<= 128 tokens). Streaming token arrival within 25ms typical and start-of-stream < 120ms.
- Concurrency/throughput: steady-state ~20 concurrent sessions for clinical UI, peak bursts to ~40 concurrent sessions for batch conversion windows. Estimated daily tokens today ~1.2M, expected to double with rollout.
- Context length: mixed — 4k typical, some clinical notes up to 16k (we'll need to support long context paths).

We attached the sample prompts and a rough architecture diagram you mentioned during the call: sample_prompts.csv, current_arch_diagram.png. Please also share any recent production traces or representative payloads if comfortable (latency_benchmarks-raw.log would help us calibrate).

Initial sizing questions for you
1) For the 16k note path, how often (percentage) does the UI require full-context generation vs. truncated prefix-only?
2) Do you need strict TLS termination inside your VPC (yes/no)?
3) Any compliance constraints around caching of prefixes or tokens?

Proposed Redwood technical path (short)
- Run a 72-hour dedicated spike: twofold approach — 1) throughput + concurrency stress with synthetic streams; 2) replay of representative traces for p95 and streaming behavior.
- GPU candidates to validate in PoC: H100 (best throughput/FP16 perf), A100 80GB (best for long-context memory), L4-class inference GPUs (cost-efficient but may require quantization and could impact streaming p95).
- Suggested starting reserved pool: 3 x H100 for streaming-heavy fast-path; add 1x A100 80GB for long-context fallbacks. We'll validate and tune autoscale/burst.

Next steps
- You: share 24–48 hour representative traces or confirm we can replay synthetic traffic.
- Redwood: we'll produce a PoC plan with concrete bench steps and cost/latency estimates by EOD Wed (Dec 2).
- Procurement: if procurement wants early numbers for budget, cc procurement@helionhealth.com and we'll include ballpark committed-costs.

Attachments: sample_prompts.csv (csv, ~8KB), current_arch_diagram.png (png, ~120KB)

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@helionhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Bianco <marco.bianco@helionhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helion Health - dedicated SLO & GPU sizing follow-up

Thanks Neha — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 16k path is used in ~12% of interactions; most sessions are under 4k. When long context is used, we can tolerate a slightly higher p95 (~300ms) provided streaming token delivery for the first tokens is fast.
- TLS termination: yes, must be inside our VPC. We run in GCP (us-west4).
- Caching: we cannot cache any PHI-sensitive prefixes for more than 30 days; short-term prefix caching (per-session) is OK.

We can provide ~48 hours of obfuscated traces — I'll have procurement and infra coordinate. Attached a small extract of traces (anonymized) on a shared Drive link; I'll send procurement separately.

One more ask: we'd like Redwood's recommendation for minimum reserved capacity that meets the p95 target without huge overcommit — ballpark cost-per-hour would be helpful for our finance team.

On timelines: we can provision a PoC environment as soon as next week if you can commit to the 72-hour validation window.

—Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Product, Clinical AI | Helion Health
maya.singh@helionhealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helion Health - dedicated SLO & GPU sizing follow-up

Hi all — quick technical readout based on Neha's notes and the anonymized snippets Maya mentioned. Putting concrete tradeoffs and a conservative starting config for the PoC.

Short answers first
- To meet 150ms p95 for <=128-token interactions with streaming start <120ms, we recommend starting with a dedicated pool of 4x H100 (FP16) or 3x H100 + 1x A100 80GB. The H100s serve the streaming fast-path; A100 provides headroom for long-context sessions and higher KV cache capacity.
- If budget is tight, 6x A100 80GB can sometimes match throughput for mixed workloads but will increase tail latency for streaming due to memory management and kernel differences. L4 is not recommended as the only class for this use case — it can be used for batch conversions and non-streaming workloads.

Why this mix
- H100: superior throughput and smaller p95 for short-context streaming due to improved tensor-core kernels and optimized multi-instance configurations.
- A100 80GB: necessary for consistent 16k context handling without chunking; useful as a fallback worker for long contexts where we avoid recompute.

Conservative PoC config (what we'll run during 72h)
- Warmup: replay of 48h anonymized traces across 6 traffic profiles (interactive short, interactive long, background batch, admin APIs, heavy charting, realtime updates).
- Baseline cluster: 3x H100 + 1x A100 80GB (reserved) with autoscale headroom of +2x H100 for 10m burst windows.
- Metrics captured: token p95, start-of-stream latency, per-session concurrency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, and end-to-end TLS handshake times.

Ballpark economics (rough on-demand numbers, final quote will vary by contract)
- 3x H100 + 1x A100 reserved (monthly committed) — estimate: $xxx/hr equivalent (we'll convert to monthly commit in PoC doc).
- Full 4x H100 reserved — ~15–20% higher compute cost, lower tail latency for streaming.

Deliverables by EOD Wed (Dec 2):
- Detailed PoC plan with exact bench steps (Aditya)
- Preliminary cost band and a recommended committed configuration (Neha)
- Docs for procurement with CAC/contract sketch (Grace)

Attachment: latency_benchmarks-raw.log (partial sample for baseline kernels)
